lean.fidelity_note: The paper fixes the zero-mean Poisson pressure and normalizes $\max_{[t_0,T]}|\mathbf a(t,0)|=\lambda^{-3/4}$. The formal statement allows any smooth periodic parent pressure satisfying the stated residual and coercivity conditions, and requires only $0<|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le\lambda^{-3/4}$. These broader hypotheses accompany a restriction: for general $V$ and $f$, zero phase average is required on all of $[0,T]$, whereas the weighted estimates concern $[t_0,T]$. Transversality, pressure normalization, and the momentum equation are imposed only on that active interval, so applying the theorem to arbitrary active-interval data requires a suitable extension. Both estimates retain exactly the $\lambda^{-1}$ gain and one extra derivative. The homogeneous leading-wave clause explicitly supplies smooth full-interval representatives agreeing with $A_1$ and its pressure on the active interval. Once the envelope exponent is fixed, the parent exponent and order constants are chosen before the parent; the exponent is independent of derivative order and depth. The verdict records these mixed hypothesis changes, not a loss of frequency decay.
